checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: close the navigation authoring gap with NavGrid schema-1 documents (to_dict/from_dict, strict validation) and nav_authoring.grid_from_boxes/read_navgrid/write_navgrid that derive blocked cells from the level's own collision AABBs with clearance inflation

impact_assessment.why: Pathfinding and following exist, but the blocked-cell set is hand-maintained beside collision boxes, so moving a wall silently desynchronizes navigation; grids also have no document form for AI inspection or authoring.
impact_assessment.benefits: One call turns level collision into a nav grid, the grid round-trips through sorted JSON, and an AI can diff or hand-edit navigation outside a running engine.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: NavGrid gains document methods, one new module, three exports and a capability; dependency: nav_authoring imports physics.AABB; concurrency: none; state: schema-1 document is new but does not touch scene snapshots.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep rasterization pure and deterministic (centre-in-inflated-box on XZ), validate every document and argument strictly, pin the clearance boundaries, and keep the canonical hash and reference PNG unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: complete the nav authoring loop by deriving collision AABBs from scene geometry (scene_boxes), skipping overlay and hidden nodes, with an optional layer filter, so a level feeds grid_from_boxes directly

impact_assessment.why: ADR-232 rasterized boxes but callers still had to collect them; scene meshes already know their world bounds, and every game would otherwise repeat the same loop with different rules for hidden and camera-relative nodes.
impact_assessment.benefits: Level collision becomes navigation input in one line, viewmodel and hidden geometry cannot leak into the walkable set, and the box order is deterministic for evidence.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: nav_authoring gains scene_boxes and one export; dependency: nav_authoring now imports culling, geometry and scene; concurrency: none; state: no document change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reuse culling.world_bounds, skip OVERLAY_LAYER unconditionally, validate the Scene and layer, pin ordering and hierarchy behaviour, prove an end-to-end pillar route, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add exact grid line-of-sight (DDA cell traversal plus the movement corner rule) and greedy path smoothing so A* routes lose redundant waypoints without ever cutting a wall corner, with a discovery flag

impact_assessment.why: A* emits a staircase even across an empty room; a simplifier that ignores walls would reintroduce exactly the failure pathfinding prevents, so the engine needs a visibility primitive first.
impact_assessment.benefits: Followers get two-point routes across open space and only the corners a wall requires, with every kept segment provably clear.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: pathfinding gains two functions, two exports and a capability; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: pure functions, no document or scene change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use exact DDA traversal instead of sampling, reject diagonal crossings with a blocked orthogonal neighbour, preserve endpoints and determinism, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add scene picking (SceneHit, raycast_scene, hit_report) that resolves the nearest visible mesh node with filters and JSON-safe reports, and fix non-unit ray distances found while wiring it

impact_assessment.why: Physics raycasts needed caller-built keyed boxes and games/AIs had no way to ask what node is under a ray; picking is a baseline Unity/Unreal capability and the bridge exposed a double-scaling defect in ray_aabb and ray_sphere for non-unit directions.
impact_assessment.benefits: One call resolves a ray to a node with distance and contact point, filters hidden/overlay/layer/ignored content, and reports hits or misses for agent logs; non-unit rays now return true world distances.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, three exports, one capability, and a behavior fix in physics for non-unit rays; dependency: picking imports culling, physics, scene; concurrency: none; state: pure queries.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reuse the same visibility and bound rules as navigation, delegate tie-breaking to physics.raycast, pin nearest hit, filters, max distance and non-unit distances with failing-first tests, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add word wrapping plus a measured paragraph draw (wrap_text, Canvas.paragraph) so HUD text wraps at the viewport width without games re-implementing layout

impact_assessment.why: The HUD had measured single-line helpers but no wrapping, so every multi-line hint or dialogue re-measured strings; this is the remaining repeated layout code after the widget work.
impact_assessment.benefits: One call draws wrapped, width-safe HUD text with newline and blank-line control and a measured height, discoverable from --describe.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: font and canvas gain functions plus a capability; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no scene or report schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Greedy word wrapping, truncation of overlong words, per-line width tests, validated scale/gap, and an unchanged canonical frame because the engine overlay does not use paragraphs yet.
